---
title: "Glossary"
subtitle: "Alphabetical reference of TimeToAlign! model terminology"
---

This page collects all terms introduced in the [Conceptual Model](concepts.qmd).
Hover over any {{< glossary glossary >}}-highlighted term elsewhere on this site
to see its definition.

For the full context in which each term is introduced, follow the cross-references
to the relevant section of the conceptual model.


## A

**AlignmentAnchor**
:   A coordinate pair associating one coordinate on timeline A with one on
    timeline B; a neutral record with no claim semantics---provenance is
    carried by the enclosing {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}. Only synchronous
    MatchClaims produce AlignmentAnchors. From a {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}
    of {{< glossary TimeIntervalEvent >}}s, one derives a **StartAnchor** and
    an **EndAnchor**.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**AlignmentBundle**
:   A collection of {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}}s with inter-group
    {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} connections; provides coordinate transfer via
    offset arithmetic, interpolation, and {{< glossary WarpMap >}}s.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**AlignmentMatrix**
:   An audio-to-audio alignment in which several recordings of one work are each
    warped onto a single shared, equidistant reference grid. Per recording, a
    parallel onset-time array gives that recording's clock-time at each grid
    column; because every array indexes the same grid they are equal length, so
    together they form a dense matrix of shape (recordings × grid columns). A
    single such file encodes an entire {{< glossary MatchGraph >}} directly ---
    every pair of recordings is related at every grid column --- rather than
    only one score-to-performance correspondence. The complete pairwise claim
    set is held in a {{< glossary MatchClaimField >}}.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

## B

**BeatGrid**
:   An ordered set of **BeatGridSegment**s and the beats they generate on a
    seconds axis. Each segment states one stretch of a recording --- an anchor
    instant, a tempo, a {{< glossary BeatPolicy >}}, and which beat of a bar
    the anchor is --- and generates beats without end; the grid orders the
    segments, bounds each by its successor's start and the last by its extent,
    and labels the resulting beats with measure and beat numbers. Each labelled
    beat is a **GridBeat**. A BeatGrid is *not* a
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} and stores nothing per beat.
    See [How to Build Beat Grids](howto/how01_beat_grids.ipynb).

**BeatPolicy**
:   How one bar is counted in beats: a grouping cycle over one counted note
    value. A 4/4 bar is four beats of a quarter, a compound 6/8 bar two beats
    of three eighths, an uneven (3+2+3)/8 bar three beats of unequal length.
    Beat lengths are derived from the grouping and the division, never stored.
    One signature admits more than one counting: a {{< glossary BeatGrid >}}'s
    lattice reads 6/8 as six beats of an eighth, because its beat-in-bar index
    counts the notated value rather than the felt pulse.

**Break**
:   A {{< glossary ControlEvent >}} that voids {{< glossary Contiguity >}}
    at its {{< glossary Instant >}}. TimeIntervals cannot span a Break,
    and Breaks cannot be inserted into existing TimeIntervals.
    See [Flow control](concepts.qmd#flow-control).

## C

**ChainMap**
:   A {{< glossary MultiMap >}} that applies multiple
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s in sequence, creating a conversion
    path from a source unit to a target unit.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Child**
:   A {{< glossary Timeline >}} nested within a parent, sharing its
    measuring unit but defining its own origin. `add_child()` locks a child
    by default, which prevents side effects from modifications. An unlocked
    child's length may change only within its parent's known length: a
    parent never grows because a child grew.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**ClaimType**
:   The semantic kind of a {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}, derived from its
    structure rather than stored --- read from whether the claim is explicit,
    whether it is synchronous, and how many of its two sides name an event.
    Six members: **event_match** (synchronous, both sides name an event; the
    case that yields {{< glossary AlignmentAnchor >}}s), **projection**
    (synchronous, exactly one side names an event, the other a bare
    coordinate), **anchor** (synchronous, neither side names an event --- two
    anonymous coordinates), **nomatch** (non-synchronous, exactly one side
    names an event whose counterpart is absent; see {{< glossary NOMATCH >}}),
    **conceptual** (non-synchronous, neither or both sides name an event ---
    a structural correspondence with no temporal commitment), and **implicit**
    (inferred by graph extension; overrides all the above).
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**CombinationMap**
:   A {{< glossary MultiMap >}} yielding outputs from multiple
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s simultaneously (e.g., *(x, y)*
    coordinate pairs).
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Commensurability**
:   Two timelines are commensurable if connected by a chain of
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s, membership in the same
    {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}}, or cross-group
    {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s, enabling coordinate translation between them.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**Commensurable**
:   See {{< glossary Commensurability >}}.

**Complete form**
:   The form in which `to_dict()` writes a
    {{< glossary "TimeSkeleton manifest" >}} by default: every key the format
    defines is written, those holding their default value included (`null`,
    `{}`, `[]`). A key whose default is its absence, such as a manifest's `id`
    or a root timeline's `offset`, is written only when it has a value. The
    complete and the {{< glossary "Minimal form" >}} of one object read back to
    equal objects, and each writes back to itself.
    See [How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles](howto/how02_group_and_bundle_files.ipynb).

**ConcatenationMap**
:   A {{< glossary MultiMap >}} combining bounded
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s such that each coordinate region is
    handled by a specific map.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Contiguity**
:   A {{< glossary TimeInterval >}} is contiguous if it monotonically
    spans all coordinates between its start and end. An
    {{< glossary Instant >}} is contiguous with a TimeInterval if it is
    synchronous with its {{< glossary EndInstant >}}.
    See [Flow control](concepts.qmd#flow-control).

**ControlEvent**
:   An event affecting flow control: either a {{< glossary Break >}}
    (voiding contiguity) or a {{< glossary Jump >}} (creating new
    contiguity).
    See [Flow control](concepts.qmd#flow-control).

**ConversionMap**
:   A typed function attached to a {{< glossary Timeline >}} that maps each
    coordinate to exactly one value (coordinate, label, or filename); also
    permits inverse conversion back to the timeline's own unit. Also called
    **C-map**.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Coordinate**
:   A position on a {{< glossary Timeline >}}, expressed as the distance
    from the origin in the timeline's measuring unit. Combines a numeric
    value with a TimeUnit. The unit alone decides the number policy:
    `quarters` and `beats` are exact `Fraction`s, discrete units (`ticks`,
    `samples`, `frames`, `pixels`) are locked to `int`, and the remaining
    continuous units (`seconds`, `points`, `centimeters`, …) are `float`.
    That declared number type is preserved at every boundary — authored,
    converted, offset-computed, interpolated, queried or retrieved — so a
    fraction-canonical axis always yields `Fraction`s and a float-canonical
    axis always yields `float`s. An explicit `number_type=` overrides the
    default, and exact input is never degraded.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## D

**DictStore**
:   A generic `EventStore` subclass holding a `dict[str, EventData]` with
    arbitrary keys. Used internally by AlignmentLoaders to store one
    `EventData` table per timeline-to-be (e.g., `"score:clt_1"`,
    `"perf:Chopin_op10_no3_p01:cpt_1"`).
    Maintains the uniform `EventStore` interface.
    See the [API reference](reference/DictStore.qmd).

**Discrete**
:   A timeline is discrete when coordinates exist only at discrete points
    (e.g., pixels, samples, ticks). Contrast with Continuous timelines
    where coordinates can take any real value (e.g., seconds, quarters).
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Domain**
:   One of three temporal categories: **Graphical** (visual/spatial),
    **Logical** (symbolic/musical), or **Physical** (audio/sound). Each
    domain has both discrete and continuous timeline variants.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## E

**element id**
:   The id that identifies a {{< glossary Timeline >}},
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}, {{< glossary Region >}}, Break,
    {{< glossary Jump >}} or {{< glossary Marker >}}. It is unique within one
    timeline tree (a root timeline and all its descendants) across every kind,
    so the id alone names the element. An id is whatever was given and is kept
    verbatim: any non-empty string without `/` and without a control
    character; spaces, colons and dots are allowed. Only an element given no
    id gets a minted one, `{prefix}_{N}` with `N` the smallest positive
    integer not yet taken in the tree. The prefix names the kind: `clt`,
    `dlt`, `cpt`, `dpt`, `cgt` or `dgt` for a timeline (continuous or
    discrete, logical, physical or graphical), `cmap`, `lmap`, `tmap` or
    `pmap` for a conversion map, and `region`, `break`, `jump` or `marker`;
    a loader role leads it (`score:clt_1`). A minted id that
    collides when its element joins a tree is re-minted; a given id that
    collides raises. The id identifies, the `name` displays: a name may be
    absent or repeat, and an id is never derived from it.

**EndInstant**
:   An {{< glossary Instant >}} marking the end of a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}. Its coordinate must be greater than or
    equal to the corresponding {{< glossary StartInstant >}}'s coordinate.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Event**
:   Anything associated with a {{< glossary Timeline >}} via
    {{< glossary Instant >}}s. An {{< glossary InstantEvent >}} has zero
    duration; a {{< glossary TimeIntervalEvent >}} has duration defined by
    start and end coordinates.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## F

**Flow**
:   One computed path through a score's control structure — the ordered
    sequence of measure visitations that results from following its repeats,
    {{< glossary Jump >}}s and voltas. A `ScoreFlowController` computes one
    from the parsed measure records, or one can be loaded from a `.flow.csv`
    ground truth and compared with `is_equivalent()`. A Flow is section-based;
    measure-count ranges follow the library's right-open `[start, end)`
    convention. It is the input a {{< glossary FlowMap >}} is built from, not
    itself a mapping between coordinates.
    See [Flow control](concepts.qmd#flow-control).

**FlowMap**
:   A path through a score's control structure (repeats, jumps), expressed as an
    ordered sequence of {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}s; not itself a
    {{< glossary Timeline >}}. Used for unfolding a score into performance
    order. A FlowMap is built from one uniform argument --- a single
    interval-like value (a {{< glossary Region >}}, a coordinate pair, a
    {{< glossary Timeline >}}, or an interval event) or an iterable of them,
    which concatenate in performance order --- or from a score's computed flow
    of {{< glossary Break >}}s and {{< glossary Jump >}}s.
    `Timeline.create_flow_map(intervals)` resolves region names against the
    timeline's own {{< glossary Region >}}s, attaches the FlowMap, and returns
    it.
    See [Derivative timelines](concepts.qmd#derivative-timelines).

## G

## I

**IdCoordinate**
:   A {{< glossary Coordinate >}} that also names the {{< glossary Timeline >}}
    it belongs to. It is the default return of every coordinate getter in the
    library — stamps, timelines, groups, bundles, match lines, graphs and warp
    maps all hand back `IdCoordinate(value, unit, timeline_id)` unless an
    explicit `format=` asks for something else. Carrying identity is what lets
    a retrieved coordinate be handed straight back as a query without restating
    which axis it came from. An IdCoordinate never compares equal to a plain
    Coordinate in either direction; use `format="coordinate"` when timeline
    identity should be discarded.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Instant**
:   Associates a {{< glossary Coordinate >}} (a "time-point") with a
    signification such as "start of event *e*". Instants sharing a
    coordinate are synchronous.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**InstantEvent**
:   An {{< glossary Event >}} defined by a single {{< glossary Instant >}},
    having zero duration.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Interval**
:   A frozen scalar pairing two plain {{< glossary Coordinate >}}s as a
    half-open span `[start, end)`: the start is inclusive, the end exclusive.
    Both endpoints must share one TimeUnit and one number type, which makes the
    interval's own `unit` and `number_type` unambiguous; its `duration` is
    exactly `end - start`, returned as a `Duration`. Reversed intervals raise;
    zero-length ones are valid. It renders through the same formatter the
    scalars use, so an interval on a `quarters` axis prints
    `[1/2, 3/2) quarters` rather than `[0.5, 1.5)`. Interval is the scalar leaf
    of interval retrieval: `TimeIntervalStamp.get_interval()` and
    `TimelineGroup.get_interval_for()` both return one.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**IntervalField**
:   The `SemanticField` paired with {{< glossary Interval >}}. It stores a
    struct of `start` and `end` coordinate structs under one `unit`, `domain`,
    and `number_type` metadata triple, materialises `Interval | None` per row,
    and exposes vectorized `start`, `end`, and `duration` accessors returning
    `CoordinateField`, `CoordinateField`, and `DurationField`.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**InverseMap**
:   The reverse transformation of a bijective
    {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

## J

**Jump**
:   A {{< glossary ControlEvent >}} with **JumpFrom** and **JumpTo**
    {{< glossary Instant >}}s. When active, makes events at JumpTo
    contiguous with those ending at JumpFrom (e.g., repeats, *dal segno*).
    Its `target` is the {{< glossary "element id" >}} of a
    {{< glossary Marker >}} of the same timeline (a segno, a coda), or `None`
    when it lands on no marker (to the start, a plain repeat); JumpTo carries
    the destination coordinate either way.
    See [Flow control](concepts.qmd#flow-control).

## L

**Length**
:   The distance between a {{< glossary Timeline >}}'s origin and its last
    {{< glossary Instant >}}, or `None` when it is not known (see
    {{< glossary "Unknown length" >}}).
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**Locked**
:   A timeline state that fixes its coordinate axis: no
    {{< glossary Instant >}}s may be added after the last time-point, so its
    length cannot change. Locking governs the coordinate axis only ---
    non-structural annotations such as {{< glossary Region >}}s may still be
    added to a locked timeline. A timeline is locked with `locked=True`, when
    `add_child()` embeds it as a {{< glossary Child >}} with its default
    `locked=True`, or after construction with `lock()`; a child read from a
    manifest keeps the manifest's `locked`. A lock cannot be lifted. A locked
    timeline's length may still be unknown. Containment does not depend on
    the lock: a child, locked or not, ends within its parent's known length,
    and content or a child added into an unlocked timeline grows that
    timeline only.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

## M

**Marker**
:   A named position in a timeline's flow control that a
    {{< glossary Jump >}} can target, such as a segno or a coda sign. A Marker
    carries an {{< glossary "element id" >}}, an optional `name`, and a
    coordinate; a Jump refers to it by its id, never by its name.
    See [Flow control](concepts.qmd#flow-control).

**Match**
:   See {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}.

**MatchfileLoader**
:   Loader for Vienna Match (`.match`) alignment files. Uses the standard
    two-step `load()` → `create_*()` pattern. A single instance processes
    all `.match` files that share the same score, building a shared score
    timeline on the first file and verifying subsequent files against it.
    Returns an {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} directly via
    `create_bundle()`. Score goes into its own group; performances
    are standalone timelines; {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s connect score to
    performances.
    See the [API reference](reference/MatchfileLoader.qmd).

**MatchClaim**
:   A claim of equivalence between events on different timelines, with
    provenance metadata (the authoring agent and a certainty). May be
    synchronous (producing {{< glossary AlignmentAnchor >}}s) or conceptual
    (structural equivalence without temporal commitment). Always knows which
    pair of timelines it connects. Four cases: (a) event-to-event,
    (b) projection, (c) {{< glossary NOMATCH >}}, (d) implicit (from group
    extension). Held individually, or columnar at scale in a
    {{< glossary MatchClaimField >}}.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchClaimField**
:   A columnar, PyArrow-backed store holding a whole set of synchronous-instant
    pairwise {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s as Arrow columns (the two timeline ids
    dictionary-encoded, each coordinate as a struct of `value`, `numerator`,
    `denominator` and `unit`) rather than as one
    frozen MatchClaim object per claim. Storing the exact ratio beside the
    float mirror is what lets a claim's coordinate come back in its axis's
    declared number type instead of being flattened on the way through the
    column. Individual MatchClaims are materialised
    on demand when a row is indexed or iterated. Built vectorized via
    `from_columns()`, it is the scalable backing for dense
    {{< glossary AlignmentMatrix >}} alignments, where the complete pairwise
    topology of a whole work runs to roughly a million claims. Shared provenance
    is held once at field level, never per row.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchGraph**
:   An auxiliary structure formed by extending {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s
    through shared coordinates; may be viewed as a hyperedge connecting
    multiple coordinates from different timelines. Connected components yield
    {{< glossary MatchStamp >}}s. Each Match box M1--M15 in the Hendrix
    figure is a MatchGraph.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchLine**
:   An ordered sequence of {{< glossary AlignmentAnchor >}}s derived from
    {{< glossary MatchClaim >}}s, sorted by coordinate on a source timeline;
    input for {{< glossary WarpMap >}} generation.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchPath**
:   A path traversal connecting matched events across multiple timelines
    (e.g., A -> B -> C), enabling indirect alignment.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MatchStamp**
:   The union of {{< glossary TimeStamp >}}s from groups synchronously
    connected by a {{< glossary MatchGraph >}}. Contains one coordinate per
    participating timeline. C-map conversion values are opt-in here: unlike
    {{< glossary TimeStamp >}}, where C-Maps are
    visible by default, `conversion_maps` on a MatchStamp getter
    (`bundle.get_matchstamp_at()`, `get_matchstamps_at()`, `get_matchstamp_table()`,
    `MatchClaim.get_matchstamp()`) defaults to `False` — across a large bundle
    they would bury the alignment answer.
    This is a per-context *default value* for a shared parameter, not a
    structural difference: MatchStamp implements the same `Stamp` interface
    as every other stamp type — `get_coordinate_for(timeline_id)` returns an
    {{< glossary IdCoordinate >}} by default and a plain number under
    `format="float"/"int"/"fraction"`, `get_unit()` converts through a C-map,
    `get_conversion_for()` reads label and structured map values,
    `present_timelines` lists available timelines, and `is_interpolated`
    identifies interpolation fallback. A stamp from any source keeps the
    identical structure, methods, and behaviour the `Stamp` contract
    guarantees; only the caller-visible default for one keyword argument
    varies by producing context.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**MeasureConstituent**
:   A measure of a measure map that is only part of its nominal measure: an
    anacrusis, or one constituent of a split measure. It carries
    `offset_within_measure`, the strictly positive quarter-note position at
    which it begins inside the nominal measure, and is the only measure class
    that does. A measure is classified as a constituent exactly when that
    offset is stated and non-zero: a shared measure number never marks a split
    measure, because alternative endings ("16a", "16b") share one too. A
    measure table states the offset in its `mc_offset` column; a Measure Map
    `.mm.json` file states none, so `MeasureMapLoader` applies the standard's
    one convention, a first row numbered 0 that is shorter than nominal being
    an anacrusis at offset nominal minus actual length. In a compressed
    measure-map row the offset is the `offset_within_measure` extension,
    written only when non-zero.

**MetricMap**
:   A table-based {{< glossary ConversionMap >}} from a quarter position to its
    measure count, built from explicit measure-boundary anchors rather than a
    uniform measure length. Correctly handles anacrusis (an incomplete first
    measure), irregular measures, varying time signatures, and repeat
    structure. Built directly from a Verovio timemap via
    `MetricMap.from_verovio_timemap()`. Not invertible — many quarters map to
    the same measure.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**MetricalPositionMap**
:   A {{< glossary CombinationMap >}} pairing a {{< glossary MetricMap >}} with
    a beat-in-measure map to return a metrical position `{mc, beat}` from a
    quarter coordinate. Adds a reverse lookup `quarters_at(mc, beat)` (metrical
    position to quarters) and `mn_at(quarters)` (quarters to measure-number
    label). Both outputs derive from the meter map, so its dictionary form
    holds `meter_map` once and names the derived beat map by `beat_map_id`,
    never the derived maps themselves.
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

**Minimal form**
:   The form in which `to_dict(minimal=True)` writes a
    {{< glossary "TimeSkeleton manifest" >}}: every key holding its default
    value is left out, except a timeline's `length`, which both forms write.
    Readers supply every default left out, so a minimal manifest can be written
    by hand; the smallest names the version and one timeline with its `id`,
    `unit` and `length`.
    See [How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles](howto/how02_group_and_bundle_files.ipynb).

**MpmLoader**
:   Loader for an MPM-Toolbox project: a sibling `.msm` score, `.mpm` modelled
    performance, and `.mpr` project file (carrying an observed audio-to-score
    alignment) for one work. Uses the standard two-step `load()` →
    `create_*()` pattern. Builds a shared logical `"score"` group holding the
    notes in two units — a ticks {{< glossary Timeline >}} (also carrying every
    MPM markup event: `Tempo`, `Dynamics`, `Articulation`, …) and a quarters
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} — with a `TicksToQuarters` map and a modelled
    quarters→seconds `TableMap` integrated from the performance's tempo markup;
    and a physical `"perf"` group of observed onsets in seconds and samples.
    Emits one synchronous cross-group {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} per score note
    (the MSM `xml:id` ↔ MPR `ref` join is a bijection). Reads the modelled
    performance and the observed alignment; never runs an aligner. Returns an
    {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} via `create_bundle()`.

**MultiMap**
:   An umbrella term for composed {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s:
    {{< glossary ChainMap >}} (sequential),
    {{< glossary CombinationMap >}} (parallel outputs), and
    {{< glossary ConcatenationMap >}} (regional).
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

## N

**NOMATCH**
:   A sentinel value in a {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} explicitly encoding the
    absence of a corresponding event on the other timeline. The MatchClaim
    records both timeline IDs but has no {{< glossary AlignmentAnchor >}}s;
    `is_synchronous` is always `False`.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

## O

**Origin**
:   The zero coordinate of a {{< glossary Timeline >}}, from which all
    positions are measured.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## P

**Parent**
:   A {{< glossary Timeline >}} that contains one or more
    {{< glossary Child >}} timelines. The parent and all its children must
    share the same measuring unit.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**PerformancePrecisionLoader**
:   Loader for audio-to-score alignment specimens: a directory bundling a
    `.solo` score, a Verovio timemap, and per-performer alignment files at the
    note, bar, and beat granularities. Uses the standard two-step `load()` →
    `create_*()` pattern. Resolves every `"<measure>+<offset>"` label to
    absolute quarters via a {{< glossary MetricMap >}}, builds one logical score
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} (quarters) and one physical performance
    {{< glossary Timeline >}} per recording (seconds), and emits a
    {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} per alignment row — synchronous for located
    onsets, {{< glossary NOMATCH >}} for the dangling ones. Returns an
    {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} via `create_bundle()`.
    See the [API reference](reference/PerformancePrecisionLoader.qmd).

**ParangonadaLoader**
:   Loader for a *parangonar* *parangonada* export: per-performance CSV triples
    (score notes, performed notes, note-level correspondences) for one work.
    Uses the standard two-step `load()` → `create_*()` pattern. Parses the
    shared score once into two logical {{< glossary Timeline >}}s (quarters and
    division-grid ticks, linked by a divs→quarters `LinearMap`), builds one
    performance group per recording with two physical {{< glossary Timeline >}}s
    (seconds and samples, linked by a `SamplesToSeconds` map), and emits one
    cross-group {{< glossary MatchClaim >}} per correspondence — synchronous for
    a matched note, {{< glossary NOMATCH >}} for a score-only or
    performance-only note. Reads the existing alignment; never runs an aligner.
    Returns an {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} via `create_bundle()`.

## R

**raw_quarters**
:   The conventional name for the {{< glossary ConversionMap >}} (specifically
    a `ShiftMap`) attached to a score timeline. The timeline stores normalised
    (non-negative) coordinates — shifted so the minimum onset is `0.0` — and
    this map converts them back to the raw quarter values of the source. Its
    offset equals `min(raw_onsets)`. Added by {{< glossary MatchfileLoader >}}
    and `PartituraLoader` so downstream code can detect and apply the same
    shift when comparing coordinates across loaders.

**Reach**
:   The farthest coordinate on a {{< glossary Timeline >}}'s own axis that its
    content reaches: the ends of its children (a {{< glossary Child >}} of
    {{< glossary "Unknown length" >}} contributing its offset plus its own
    reach), {{< glossary Region >}} ends, {{< glossary Break >}} and
    {{< glossary Marker >}} coordinates, both ends of every
    {{< glossary Jump >}}, and the end of the measure map. Events are not part
    of it. A timeline without such content reaches 0. The reach is independent
    of the length; displays use it as the extent of a timeline of unknown
    length. Read it as `Timeline.reach`.

**Region**
:   A part of a {{< glossary Timeline >}} defined by a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}, identified by its
    {{< glossary "element id" >}} and displayed by its `name` (e.g.,
    "Chorus", "Verse"). Regions are not timelines and cannot hold events or
    maps directly.
    See [Regions](concepts.qmd#regions).

**Root**
:   The top-level {{< glossary Timeline >}} in a hierarchy of nested
    timelines. No parent bounds its length; an unlocked descendant grows
    only within its parent's known length, never pushing its parent.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**RotationMap**
:   A periodic {{< glossary ConversionMap >}} that wraps coordinates
    cyclically (e.g., an ostinato part that repeats while the main
    timeline advances).
    See [Conversion maps](concepts.qmd#conversion-maps).

## S

**Segment**
:   A {{< glossary Child >}} timeline that is contiguous with its
    siblings. Segments enable concatenation of local coordinate systems.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**SegmentLine**
:   A runtime class parameterized by its segment class, such as
    `SegmentLine[DiscreteGraphicalTimeline]`, whose contiguous
    {{< glossary Segment >}}s tile its full length. A line is also an instance
    of that segment class. Any timeline can check the structure with
    `is_segment_line()` and adopt enforcement with `as_segment_line()`; a line
    returns to an unenforced timeline with `to_timeline()`; both return a
    copy. Use `create_children_from_boundaries()` for boundary-driven tiling.
    Appending extends an unlocked line, while appending to a locked line
    raises `RuntimeError`. The segments of a line of known length keep
    ending at its length: a segment with a successor ends at the successor's
    offset, the last one at the line's end, and changing a segment's length
    never moves the line's end. A segment of unknown length ends at its
    successor's offset, or, the last one, at the line's known length.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**StartInstant**
:   An {{< glossary Instant >}} marking the start of a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**SupportPolicy**
:   How a cross-timeline {{< glossary MatchStamp >}} treats a timeline whose
    transferred coordinate falls outside *alignment support* --- the entering
    coordinate lies beyond the transferring {{< glossary WarpMap >}}'s anchor
    hull, or the produced coordinate would fall outside the target timeline's
    `[0, length]` span. `omit` (the default) drops that timeline; `clamp`
    reports the nearest in-support boundary coordinate; `extrapolate` keeps the
    linear extrapolation clipped to `[0, length]`. No policy ever yields a
    negative coordinate, and the queried timeline's own coordinate is never
    altered. Set per call on
    `AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamp_at(..., support_policy=...)` or persistently
    via `AlignmentBundle.support_policy`.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**Synchrony**
:   *Strict synchrony*: {{< glossary Instant >}}s sharing identical
    coordinates. *Pragmatic synchrony*: Instants binned together based on
    a threshold (e.g., for quantisation).
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

## T

**TimeInterval**
:   Defined by a {{< glossary StartInstant >}} and
    {{< glossary EndInstant >}}; left-inclusive and right-exclusive
    [*s*, *e*). The EndInstant's coordinate must be >= the StartInstant's.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**TimeIntervalEvent**
:   An {{< glossary Event >}} with duration, defined by a
    {{< glossary TimeInterval >}}. Contrast with
    {{< glossary InstantEvent >}}.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**TimeIntervalStamp**
:   Combination of a start {{< glossary TimeStamp >}} and an end
    TimeStamp, representing a cross-section of an interval through the
    timeline hierarchy. It stores one {{< glossary Interval >}} per timeline
    ID; `get_interval(timeline_id)` returns that Interval, `get_intervals()`
    the whole mapping, `get_duration_for()` an `IdDuration`, and
    `get_interval_in(unit)` the span converted through a C-map. Interval
    retrieval takes no `format` argument — its scalar leaf is always an
    Interval.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

**Timeline**
:   A positive coordinate axis defined by an origin and a measuring unit;
    continuous (real) or discrete (integer). Accommodates events and
    potentially {{< glossary Child >}} timelines.
    See [Foundations](concepts.qmd#foundations).

**TimelineGroup**
:   An array of member timelines that share the same graphical start and
    end: every member's 0 coincides with every other member's 0, and every
    member's length with every other member's length. Placing timelines in a
    group asserts {{< glossary Commensurability >}} regardless of their
    units. A position in between converts linearly and exactly (`p` on
    member A is `p · len_B / len_A` on member B) and is written in the target
    member's number type. When only part of a timeline takes part, the member
    is a {{< glossary Child >}} of that timeline at its exact offset; a member
    is never placed partially. No member is an ancestor or a descendant of
    another member of the same group, since a child sits at its offset inside
    its parent. A group answers with the same
    {{< glossary TimeStamp >}} class as a {{< glossary Timeline >}};
    `to_dict()` and `from_dict()` write and read it with every timeline it
    needs.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#alignment).

**TimeSkeleton manifest**
:   The JSON file format in which timelines, groups and bundles are exchanged,
    one shape for all: the version marker `"timeskeleton"`, an array of root
    `timelines`, and optionally the manifest's `id`, `name` and `meta`, its
    `groups` and its `graphical` (display order and styling). A single
    timeline is a manifest of one root, a group a manifest with one group; a
    manifest with an `id` or a `name` is named. Every manifest is an
    alignment bundle, also one holding one timeline or one group, and a
    manifest with neither an `id` nor a `name` is an anonymous bundle. A
    value on a timeline's own axis (`length`, a child's `offset`, region
    bounds, flow-control coordinates) is written bare, in the axis's number
    type.
    {{< glossary Timeline >}}, {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}} and
    {{< glossary AlignmentBundle >}} write one with `to_dict()` and read one
    with `from_dict()`. The library class `TimeSkeleton` is a different
    thing: a temporal structure shared by the timelines of one work.
    See [How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles](howto/how02_group_and_bundle_files.ipynb).

**TimeStamp**
:   A cross-section through a timeline or group at a given coordinate,
    capturing positions in all connected systems plus values converted by
    all attached {{< glossary ConversionMap >}}s. It stores one
    {{< glossary Coordinate >}} per timeline ID, so each entry carries its own
    unit and number type. TimeStamp implements the `Stamp` interface it
    shares with {{< glossary MatchStamp >}}: a typed `axis`,
    `get_coordinate_for()` and
    `get_coordinates_for()` returning {{< glossary IdCoordinate >}}s by
    default, `get_unit()` for unit conversion, `get_conversion_for()` for
    label and structured map values, `present_timelines`, and
    `is_interpolated`. A bare number is an explicit
    `format="float"/"int"/"fraction"` request; there is no ambient float view.
    See [Nested timelines](concepts.qmd#nested-timelines).

## U

**Unknown key**
:   A key of a {{< glossary "TimeSkeleton manifest" >}} that the format does
    not define, written by another application for its own use. The library
    keeps every unknown key on the object read from the JSON object it was
    found in and writes it back in place.

**Unknown length**
:   A timeline length of `None` (`null` in a manifest), stating that the
    length is not known. It is a fact, never inferred from content, and any
    timeline may have it: root, {{< glossary Child >}},
    {{< glossary Locked >}}, group member or {{< glossary Segment >}}.
    Positions on such a timeline are not bounded above, unless its parent
    ends it, as a segment line ends a {{< glossary Segment >}}; an operation
    that needs the end raises {{< glossary UnknownLengthError >}}. Setting a length
    to or from `None` is an ordinary edit; `Timeline.is_length_known` tells
    which case holds, and displays use the {{< glossary Reach >}}.

**UnknownLengthError**
:   The `ValueError` raised by an operation that needs the end of a timeline
    whose length is unknown, before it changes anything. Its message names the
    operation and the timeline; group conversion to or from such a member and
    appending a child at such a parent's end are examples.

## W

**WarpMap**
:   An interpolation-based coordinate mapping derived from a
    {{< glossary MatchLine >}}; enables non-linear coordinate transfer
    between {{< glossary TimelineGroup >}}s. It declares both axes — source
    and target unit *and* number type — and is queried through
    `get_coordinate_at(position)` for one position or
    `get_coordinates_at([...])` for a batch; the object is not callable and
    exposes no raw arrays. `inverse()` returns a WarpMap with both units and
    both number types swapped.
    See [Alignment](concepts.qmd#coordinate-transfer).
